title: in_tcp is broken on Windows for 2.0.x (2.0.6)
body:
## Bug Report

**Describe the bug**
The tcp input plugin is not processing json payloads correctly in 2.0.x. After the first payload json message it appears to hang and fluent-bit requires multiple ctrl-c to exit. This works as expected in the 1.x versions of fluent-bit.

**To Reproduce**
fluent-bit executable is downloaded from https://fluentbit.io/releases/2.0/fluent-bit-2.0.6-win64.zip

Start fluent-bit with the tcp input and stdout plugin
C:\fluent-bit-2.0.6-win64\bin>fluent-bit.exe -v -i tcp -o stdout

Now send a json payload to be processed by fluent-bit using chocolatey provided netcat using the command below
`echo {"key 1": 123456789, "key 2": "abcdefg"}  | C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\lib\netcat\tools\nc.exe -w 1 localhost 5170
`
Any succeeding payloads are not processed by the fluent-bit by e.g. by executing the command above a second time.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
The root cause of the issue is that [prepare_destroy_conn](https://github.com/fluent/fluent-bit/blob/master/src/flb_downstream.c#L191) which is the inner downstream function used to dispose of connections (ie. when they are closed)  was not using the right approach to determine if it should remove the connection from the event loop or not which in turn caused the event loop to continuously return (due to the now closed socket being present in its list of sockets to monitor) which looked like a deadlock from a users perspective (fluent-bit wouldn't handle other events) but was more like a denial of service which could be observed by the elevated CPU usage.

I'll open a PR to fix the issue in fluent-bit 2.1 and 2.0 today.
